results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
This is a 4-color control brew (blue, red, white, black). It started from the Jeskai Control deck that already runs Resonating Lute; I added black for Inevitable Defeat. No published list runs all three of your cards together.

**The plan:** Lightning Helix, No More Lies, Get Lost, Seam Rip and Day of Judgment keep you alive through the early turns against Prowess and Landfall. On turn 4 you play Resonating Lute. After that, every land taps for two mana of any one color for instants and sorceries.

- **Inevitable Defeat** needs black, which is hard in a Jeskai mana base. With the Lute out, any land can pay for it. It can't be countered, exiles a permanent, and makes them lose 3 life while you gain 3.
- **Jeskai Revelation** normally costs 7. With the Lute, four lands are enough to cast it: return a card to its owner's hand, deal 4 damage, make two 1/1 Monk tokens, draw two cards and gain 4 life.
- **Flashback** lets you spend your leftover Lute mana to recast Revelation or Defeat from your graveyard in the same turn.

You win by draining them with Revelation, Defeat and Helix while keeping the board clear.

**Why this direction:** I looked at three options:
1. This Jeskai Control base with black added.
2. A Lute deck built on the Lessons package.
3. A Mardu creature deck adding blue.

I picked the first because the Lute does two jobs there at once: it gives you black for Defeat and enough mana for Revelation. A proven Lute Jeskai Control list just went 5-0 in a Standard League.

**Mana:** 26 lands. 
- **Black:** 4 real black lands (Godless Shrine, Watery Grave, Nomad Outpost, Multiversal Passage), plus 4 Great Hall of the Biblioplex. Great Hall can make any color, but only for instants and sorceries.
- **Other colors:** the deck checker counted 18 white, 19 blue and 14 red sources (Great Hall included). That matches the stock Jeskai Control mana.

**Honest odds:**
- **Lute:** you'll have one by turn 5 on the play 56.6% of the time, before counting Consult the Star Charts and Stock Up digging for it.
- **Black:** you'll have a source by then 82.4% of the time.
- **Full line:** drawing all five cards in the listed win line by turn 9 happens only 3.2% of the time. The deck never needs all five, though. Lute plus either payoff is enough.
- **Revelation copies:** I run 3 instead of 4 because two 7-drops in your opening hand are dead without the Lute. Flashback works as a fourth.

**Sideboard:** built for the matchups that show up most:
- Fire Magic and Pyroclasm against Prowess and Elementals.
- Disdainful Stroke, Negate and Voice of Victory against Dimir and the mirror.
- Rest in Peace against graveyard decks.
- Tishana's Tidebinder against creature abilities.

--- After review ---
I made the reviewer's swap: **3 Stock Up out, 3 Three Steps Ahead in.** The deck was accepted, with no other changes to the main deck or sideboard.

- **Why the swap is right:** Stock Up is a 3-mana sorcery, so casting it means spending your own turn's mana instead of holding up No More Lies, Lightning Helix or Inevitable Defeat. Three Steps Ahead is a 1-mana instant where you pay extra for each effect you choose: {1}{U} to counter a spell, {2} to draw two and then discard one. You can hold it up on the opponent's turn and use it as either effect.
- **How it works with Lute:** Lute's double mana pays for instants, so with Lute out you can usually afford both the counter and the draw at once.
- **Bonus:** Its third option ({3}) makes a copy of an artifact you control. That gives you a backup Lute if the first one gets destroyed.
- **Does the plan change?** No. The deck still survives the early turns with Helix and counterspells and lands Lute on turn 4. From there it casts two Inevitable Defeats in a turn, then Jeskai Revelation and Flashback, aiming to win around turn 7. Three Steps Ahead adds one more counterspell to protect Revelation.

The checker reported that you'll have drawn every card in the win line by turn 7 in only 0.7% of games. That number is misleading, because the deck doesn't need all six cards. In practice it only needs Lute plus a finisher (Defeat or Revelation), and the card draw helps find them.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
I built a four-color (white, blue, red, green) infinite combo deck. The Jolly Balloon Man copies a Merfolk that untaps other Merfolk, over and over, until you have unlimited mana and unlimited hasty flying tokens. This is a brew: no published list in the last 400 days plays your three cards together.

**The combo (found by searching the card pool):**
1. **Set up.** Get Forensic Researcher ("{T}: Untap another target permanent you control") and Deepway Navigator (flash; when it enters, it untaps each other Merfolk you control) onto the battlefield. Neither one needs to have been in play since your last turn.
2. **Make two Researchers.** Balloon Man pays {1} to make a hasty copy of Researcher, and that copy taps to untap Balloon Man. Do it once more. You now have two tapped Researcher copies, both Merfolk.
3. **The loop.** Balloon Man pays {1} to copy Navigator. The copy's enter trigger untaps both Researcher copies. One untaps Balloon Man. The other untaps Bloom Tender, which makes one mana per color you control (usually 4). Each loop gains you 3 mana and leaves a hasty 1/1 flying Navigator copy.
4. **Win.** Repeat as many times as you like, then attack with all the flyers.

**What each requested card does:**
- **Balloon Man** is the engine.
- **Bloom Tender** speeds up your setup and turns the loop into unlimited mana. Without it, Researcher can untap the land you tapped instead, so the loop breaks even and still makes as many tokens as you want.
- **Sewer-veillance Cam** costs one blue mana and has flash. It can untap Balloon Man for a second copy in the same turn, untap Bloom Tender for a burst of mana, or tap down an attacker or blocker. When it leaves, you get that tap or untap again.

**Directions I considered:**
- A Selesnya Offense–style creature deck that uses Balloon Man to copy enters-the-battlefield creatures for value.
- A Simic Omniscience–style deck built around Formidable Speaker.
- The Merfolk untap combo.

I chose the combo because it's the only one with a real line to winning the game. I took Formidable Speaker from the Simic Omniscience list as the tutor, and the Llanowar Elves and green dual lands from the Aang list. Speaker discards a card to find any creature. Balloon Man can also copy Speaker: the copy finds another piece and can pay {1} to untap Balloon Man, so you can gather the rest of the combo in one turn.

**Honest odds:** The checker says you'll have drawn every card in the line naturally by turn 5 in only about 6% of games. That doesn't count the four Speakers, or the fact that the loop runs without Bloom Tender. Expect most wins on turns 5–7.

**Mana:** The mana base has 15 green sources, against about 21 in Aang lists. That's the price of playing four colors; Bloom Tender helps make up for it.

**Interaction:** The main deck has Burst Lightning, Get Lost and Seam Rip. The sideboard has counterspells, extra removal and Rest in Peace, aimed at Prowess, Lessons, control and graveyard decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I built a Boros Dwarves equipment aggro deck (22 lands, average mana value 1.84). It's a **brew**: no published list in the last 400 days plays these three cards together, so there was no proven version to copy.

**The plan:** Play Dwarven Mauler on turn 1 and Kíli on turn 2. On turn 3, cast Hard-Won Jitte: Kíli draws a card, and the Jitte's equip {2} costs {0} on Mauler because of Mauler's discount. That gives you a turn-3 double striker. Dwarven Mattock attaches to a Dwarf for free when it enters (+2/+2, ward 1), so Mauler becomes a 4/3 double striker hitting for 8. Dáin's Company looks at the top four cards for the next Dwarf or Equipment and gains lifelink while you control another Dwarf. Burst Lightning clears blockers or finishes the game.

**How likely the line is:** About 43% of the time you have Kíli plus an equipment piece by turn 3, and 67% of the time you have a cheap target (Mauler or Giott) plus equipment. Dáin's Company's dig and Kíli's draws push those numbers up. The checker says only 0.5% of games have all six named line cards by turn 5, but that's the odds of drawing those exact six cards. The deck has backups for each role: Giott already has double strike, Dáin Ironfoot comes with his own Axe and gives equipped attackers double strike, Thorin gives your artifacts and creatures ward, and Mjölnir doubles damage and equips any legendary red or white creature (Kíli, Giott, Thorin, Bofur, Dáin) for {1}.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Boros Dwarves equipment with the Boros Aggro burn package** (chosen).
2. **Fitting the Dwarves into the Boros Weapons artifact shell.** That deck is built around artifact engines like Weapons Manufacturing and United Battlefront, not creatures carrying equipment, so it would push your three cards aside. I only borrowed its two-color lands.
3. **A Selesnya or Naya creature shell from the menu's Selesnya Offense deck.** Those cards don't support Dwarves or equipment at all.

I chose the first because Mauler, Kíli and Dáin's Company each reward exactly one thing: cheap Dwarves plus cheap equipment. A full tribal deck triggers all three every game.

**Choices worth knowing:**
- **22 lands.** The checker pointed out that Boros Weapons lists run about 25, but that deck has a much higher curve. 22 suits this curve; Boros Aggro, the closer comparison, averages about 23.
- **Fewer copies of some cards.** Mjölnir and Dáin Ironfoot run 2 each and Thorin runs 3. They're legendary and more expensive than the rest of the curve, so extra copies would often get stuck in hand.
- **Sideboard.** It targets the top decks:
  - Sear, Lightning Helix and Abrade against Prowess and Elementals.
  - Ghost Vacuum and Rest in Peace against Dimir Excruciator, Reanimator and Lessons.
  - Shattered Acolyte (also a Dwarf) and Authority of the Consuls for artifact and enchantment threats and go-wide decks.

--- After review ---
I made the reviewer's fix as suggested, and the resubmitted deck was accepted.

**What changed:**
- **Cut 2 Sundown Pass.** It enters tapped unless you control two or more other lands, so it's a tapped land on turns 1–2. Those are the turns you need to cast Dwarven Mauler ({R}) and then Kíli ({1}{W}). The deck's other dual lands stay in.
- **Added 1 Plains.** That brings the deck down to 21 lands (5 Mountain, 4 Plains, 4 Sacred Foundry, 4 Inspiring Vantage, 4 Sunbillow Verge), which is enough for a curve this low. The extra Plains keeps white mana steady for Kíli and Bofur.
- **Added a third Bofur, Reliable Guardian.** It costs {W}, it's a 1/1 Dwarf with lifelink, and it can carry equipment. It also counts toward Kíli's draw and storied, and it's another hit for Dáin's Company's look at the top four cards. Its Adventure side, Concerted Care ({1}{W}), gives hexproof and indestructible until end of turn, which can save a fully equipped Mauler. Bofur is legendary, so I stopped at 3 copies to make drawing a second one less likely.

The way the deck wins hasn't changed. Mauler pays {2} less for equips that target it, so Hard-Won Jitte's equip {2} costs nothing and gives it double strike. Dwarven Mattock attaches itself to a Dwarf when it enters, for +2/+2 and ward {1}. Together they make Mauler a 4/3 double striker that hits for 8.

The submission tool reports that you'll have drawn all six cards in that sequence by turn 5 in only about 1% of games. That number counts every specific card in the chain, and it doesn't count card draw or tutors. Kíli's draws and Dáin's Company's search cover a lot of that gap, but plenty of real games will end on a different equipped Dwarf rather than this exact line.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built an Orzhov (white-black) Aristocrats brew. Aristocrats decks make lots of small tokens and sacrifice them for value. The deck was accepted with no errors or warnings.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-black tokens** using the Mono-Black Aggro shell (Bitterbloom Bearer, Lord Skitter).
2. **Golgari Food**, borrowing the Golgari Roots deck where Zealot already shows up.
3. **Orzhov Aristocrats**, borrowing Mardu Discard's mana base and Voice of Victory.

I chose the third because it adds the two strongest payoffs I found for sacrificing tokens, Vito and Kambal, plus Tolls of War, a token maker that keeps going every turn.

**How the three cards work together:**
- **Greedy Freebooter** is turn-one fodder that leaves a Treasure behind when it dies.
- **The Sackville-Bagginses** is the engine. Every token you sacrifice makes the opponent lose 1 life, and that includes Treasures spent for mana and Clues you crack.
- **Umbral Collar Zealot** is the free outlet: it turns any spare token into 1 damage plus a surveil.
- The rest of the deck feeds them tokens:
  - Voice of Victory makes two Warriors every attack. Sacrifice them after combat for 2 drains, and opponents can't cast spells on your turn.
  - Bitterbloom Bearer makes a Faerie every turn.
  - Tolls of War makes a Clue, then an Ally on each turn you sacrifice something.
  - Kambal drains 1 whenever your tokens enter.
- **Vito** is the finisher. Sacrifice three times in one turn and you gain 2 life, the opponent loses 2, and you get a 4/3 flyer, on top of the Sackville drains.
- Main-deck removal is 4 Erode, 4 Requiting Hex and 1 Get Lost. The sideboard is aimed at the decks in the menu.

**Odds:** Drawing every card in the full line by turn 6 is only 1.3%, but the deck doesn't need the exact sequence because the pieces overlap. By turn 4, about 75% of games have both a token maker and either Sackville or Zealot, which is enough to start the drain engine.

**Assumptions:**
- No list in the results plays these three cards together, so this is untested.
- I used 22 lands because the curve is so low (average mana value 1.95).

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
I built a Jeskai Superfriends brew, a deck that wins mostly with planeswalkers. It uses the mana base and blue card draw/counters from the Jeskai Control lists that already run Ajani Unrelenting. The check found no legality or rules problems.

**The plan:** On turn 2, play Gideon's Memorial or Solitary Cell. You'll have one of the 8 copies by turn 2 in about 71% of games. Memorial's mana can only be spent on planeswalkers, which lets each of your 13 planeswalkers come down a turn early. It also gives your creature tokens +1/+0 and vigilance. Solitary Cell exiles the opponent's best permanent with mana value 3 or less. Later it lets you discard extra legendary cards (spare planeswalkers or a second Memorial) to draw.

Ajani Unrelenting is the finisher. Every time you activate a loyalty ability, it makes a 2/2 Cadet, and Elspeth, Storm Slayer doubles that to two Cadets. Its −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your own tokens, which clears the board while your army stays. Its +1 gives everything +1/+0 and haste for the lethal attack.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Boros tokens:** Memorial pumps tokens from Elspeth, Ajani, Outland Chaperone and Quintorius Kand. The problem is that red and white have no real card draw.
2. **A package from the Boros Dragons menu deck:** It doesn't fit. Its Clarion Conqueror would shut off Memorial's mana ability, and dragons don't use Memorial's token bonus.
3. **Jeskai Superfriends (chosen):** It keeps the white-red core that all three of your cards need. Blue adds Stock Up, No More Lies and The Theorist, Jace Beleren for card draw and protection, and the walker lineup has already gone 5-0 in a Standard League.

**Things to know:**
- **Fewer blue sources than usual:** The deck has 13 blue sources, while Jeskai Control lists average about 19. That's on purpose: white and red are the main colors here and blue is a splash. Memorial's any-color mana also helps you cast Jace.
- **Ajani timing:** You'll have Ajani Unrelenting in hand by turn 6 in about half of games (3 copies). I kept it at 3 because it's a legendary 6-drop. Memorial still gets 4 copies, since extras become a 4-damage removal spell or something to discard to Cell.
- **The full win line is rare:** Every card in the five-card line is drawn by turn 7 in only about 3% of games. You don't need all of them. Any planeswalker plus Memorial pressures the opponent, and Ajani and Elspeth are just the strongest finish.

**Sideboard:**
- Voice of Victory and Flashfreeze for Boros Dragons, Elementals and other aggressive red decks
- Rest in Peace for Jund Sacrifice and Reanimator
- Pinnacle Starcage, Seam Rip and a second Day of Judgment against decks full of cheap cards or that flood the board with creatures
- Disdainful Stroke and Spell Snare for control mirrors

--- After review ---
I took the reviewer's fix. The deck was accepted with no warnings.

**What changed:**
- **Main deck: −1 Day of Judgment, +1 Get Lost.** The reviewer was right. Day of Judgment says "Destroy all creatures," so it would kill the Kithkin, Soldiers and Cadets the whole plan is built on. Ajani Unrelenting's −3 already clears the board without touching my tokens. Get Lost costs {1}{W}, is an instant, and destroys a creature, enchantment or planeswalker. That covers a lot of threats and leaves my board alone. The downside: it gives the opponent two Map tokens.
- **Sideboard:** I kept the one Day of Judgment there for matchups where the opponent floods the board with creatures and I'm behind.

Nothing else changed: same 60 cards otherwise, same mana, same win line (Memorial → Solitary Cell → Ajani, Outland Chaperone → Elspeth → Ajani Unrelenting). I submitted it with a target of turn 6, which is a turn later than the turn-5 finish the line describes.

**Odds:** You'll draw all five cards in the line by turn 6 in only about 2% of games. You don't need all five, though. Any two of the token planeswalkers plus Memorial's mana and token boost usually build a big enough board. Elspeth doubles the tokens but isn't required.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Slumbering Trudge, Fight Rigging and The Great Henge.
results.text:
I built **Mono-Green Trudge Rigging**, a mono-green ramp deck that runs on dork mana. It's a brew: no published list in any format plays all three of your cards together.

**How the three cards work together**
- **Slumbering Trudge is not meant to attack.** For X=0 it costs just {G} and comes in tapped and stunned, but it's still a 6/6. That power is what matters.
- **Fight Rigging** puts a +1/+1 counter on Trudge at your combat step. Trudge is now 7 power, so you get to play the card Rigging hid away for free. That's usually Craterhoof Behemoth, Emrakul, the Promised End, another Henge or Ouroboroid.
- **The Great Henge** costs {X} less, where X is your biggest creature's power. Next to a 7-power Trudge it costs only {G}{G}. From then on, every creature you play gets a counter and draws you a card.

**The plan**
- Turn 1: an elf.
- Turn 2: Trudge, plus Badgermole Cub or Raucous Audience. Trudge's 6 power turns on Audience's {G}{G} mode.
- Turn 3: Fight Rigging and Henge in the same turn.
- Turn 5: kill. Ouroboroid spreads counters across your board, then Craterhoof or Tyvar finishes. Tyvar's pump gives the team +X/+X, where X is Trudge's 7 power.
- If you need cards, Life's Legacy can sacrifice the stunned Trudge to draw 6.

**Directions I considered**
1. **Mono-green ramp (chosen).** It borrows the elves + Badgermole Cub + Ouroboroid package from Selesnya Company and Mono-Green Devotion.
2. **Golgari.** Trudge and Rigging backed by Fatal Push and Thoughtseize.
3. **Selesnya Company.** Collected Company can find Trudge, since it counts as a 1-drop.

I picked the first because every extra power and every extra creature there feeds both Rigging and Henge. The other two spend slots on cards that do neither. The closest real deck, Modern's Fanatic Eldrazi (Trudge + Rigging), relies on Fanatic of Rhonas and other cards that aren't legal in Pioneer. So Raucous Audience fills Fanatic's role, and the 21-land mana base comes from Mono-Green Devotion. check_deck found no problems with it.

**Odds without mulligans**
- Trudge and Fight Rigging both in hand by turn 3: about 22%.
- Trudge plus either Rigging or Henge by turn 4: about 38%.
- The listed turn-5 line needs one specific set of cards, so assembling all of them only happens about 0.1% of the time. In practice the deck wins with substitutes. Ouroboroid's counters or Rigging on Outcaster Trailblazer can also reach 7 power, and the dorks can hard-cast your big cards.

**Sideboard**
- Graveyard hate for Greasefang and Phoenix.
- Artifact and enchantment removal for Cutter, Talent and Annex.
- Polukranos Reborn against the red decks.
- Hexproof spells to protect your key creature from removal.

--- After review ---
I made both of the reviewer's suggested changes. The revised deck is accepted and still 60 cards.

1. **Emrakul, the Promised End → second Craterhoof Behemoth.** A mono-green deck only puts about 2 card types in the graveyard, so Emrakul's discount ({1} per card type) leaves it costing around 11. That makes it a dead draw unless Fight Rigging hides it. And when it does come in free, it takes over the opponent's next turn instead of winning on the spot. Craterhoof has haste and gives your whole team trample and +X/+X, where X is the number of creatures you control. In a deck full of dorks that's a kill whether it comes in free off Fight Rigging or gets hard-cast for 8 with Badgermole Cub-doubled dorks, Nykthos or Henge mana.

2. **2 Life's Legacy → 2 more Outcaster Trailblazer (now 4).** The card you'd most want to sacrifice to Life's Legacy is Slumbering Trudge. But Trudge is what reaches 7 power for Fight Rigging, makes The Great Henge cheaper, and turns on Raucous Audience. Trading it for cards shuts the engine down. Trailblazer gives a mana when it enters, draws a card whenever a creature with power 4 or more enters (Trudge, Ouroboroid, Craterhoof), and is itself a 4-power body that makes Henge cheaper. You get the card draw without giving anything up.

The win line is the same: dork, then Trudge, then Fight Rigging and Henge, then Ouroboroid, then Craterhoof. It's meant to finish around turn 5.

One caution: the submission check put the chance of having drawn every card in that full line by turn 5 at only 0.2%. That check doesn't count the cards the deck draws along the way, but I haven't checked how often it really wins by turn 5. The pieces do overlap, though. Raucous Audience can fill in for Badgermole Cub, Llanowar Elves is one of 8 one-mana dorks, and Fight Rigging can hide whichever of Henge, Ouroboroid or Craterhoof is missing.

results.text:
I built a Mono-White Heroic deck (a brew) around Favored Hoplite, Phalanx Leader and cheap spells that target your own creatures. All three of your cards are in at 4 copies.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-White Heroic.** In recent results, all three of your cards show up together in just two lists, both Mono-White.
2. **Azorius Heroic.** This takes the blue protection package from the 3-list Azorius Heroic deck (Slip Out the Back, Shore Up, Secret Identity).
3. **Boros.** This takes Monstrous Rage and Emberheart Challenger from the Prowess decks on your menu.

I went with Mono-White. Your three cards are all white sorceries, and Phalanx Leader and Fabled Hero need {W}{W}. White also has its own Lessons for Guiding Voice to fetch, so the deck can play 19 Plains-type lands and skip the shaky dual-land mana. The only menu cards I borrowed are Greasefang's Sheltered by Ghosts and Eiganjo.

**The plan:**
- **Turns 1–2:** Play Favored Hoplite, then Phalanx Leader or Illuminator Virtuoso.
- **Growing the board:** Each 1-mana spell you aim at a heroic creature triggers it. Pointed at Phalanx Leader, the trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every creature you control. Guiding Voice also Learns: it fetches Enter the Avatar State, Reduce to Memory or another Lesson from your sideboard.
- **Practiced Offense is the finisher.** Target yourself for the team-wide counters and target Leader as the creature. Leader's heroic trigger adds a second counter to everything, and you give double strike to your biggest attacker. Next turn, flash it back for {1}{W} to do it again.
- **Protection:** Gods Willing, Sheltered by Ghosts and Light the Way protect your key creature, and they trigger heroic too.

**Odds:**
- By turn 2 you'll have a heroic creature plus a targeting spell about 93% of the time.
- By turn 3 you'll have Practiced Offense about 49% of the time.
- The checker says you'll draw every card in my example win line by turn 5 only about 3% of the time. That number doesn't mean much, because the deck doesn't need that exact sequence: 17 creatures and 24 targeting spells can stand in for each other.

**Things to know:**
- **19 lands is low on purpose.** The check flagged that Mono-White decks average about 23 lands. That figure comes from the Humans/Mutavault version. This deck's average mana value is 1.63, which is close to the 19–20 lands Azorius Heroic runs. Flashback cards and Abandoned Air Temple give you something to do with extra mana.
- **Six sideboard slots are Lessons for Guiding Voice to fetch.** The other nine are aimed at the field: Rest in Peace for Phoenix and Greasefang, Spectacular Tactics for Sheoldred-type threats, and Elite Spellbinder, Light of Hope and Declaration in Stone.

--- After review ---
I made both of the reviewer's fixes, and the revised deck was accepted at 60 cards with no warnings.

1. **Light the Way out, 2 Defiant Strike in.** Defiant Strike costs W, gives a creature +1/+0 and draws a card. It sets off heroic and Phalanx Leader just like Light the Way did, but it replaces itself, which matters in a deck that runs out of cards fast. Light the Way's +1/+1 counter and untap, or its bounce mode, did little in a deck that just attacks every turn. Defiant Strike is also the one card here showing up in current lists, in 3 Azorius Heroic decks over the last 90 days.

2. **Lagonna-Band Trailblazer out, 2 Akroan Skyguard in.** Skyguard costs 1W and is a 1/1 flier that gets a +1/+1 counter each time you target it. Trailblazer was a 0/4 for W, so counters on it just made a bigger wall. A flier turns the counters from Phalanx Leader and the double strike from Practiced Offense into damage over blockers. The cost is one more 2-drop competing with Leader and Illuminator Virtuoso. I accepted that because 4 Favored Hoplite still give you a turn-1 play.

The plan to win hasn't changed: Hoplite, then Phalanx Leader, then cheap spells aimed at Leader so every creature gets counters. Practiced Offense, plus its flashback the next turn, adds more counters and double strike, and Gods Willing protects the key creature. The deck now has 24 cheap spells that target your own creatures and 17 heroic creatures to aim them at.

The check said you'll have drawn every card in that exact sequence by turn 5 in only 0.7% of games. That figure is much stricter than how the deck actually plays. In practice you only need one heroic creature, ideally Leader, plus a few targeting spells, so the deck doesn't depend on hitting that exact sequence.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Tolarian Terror, Bushwhack and Eddymurk Crab.
results.text:
I built this as a **Simic (blue-green) Terror tempo brew**: a cheap-spells deck where Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab come down as 1–3 mana 5/5s and Bushwhack acts as a one-mana removal spell. No published deck plays all three cards together. I borrowed the closest real shell, the Izzet Crab list from a May Pioneer Challenge (10th place, 4–2).

**The three directions I considered**
1. **Simic tempo.** Blue cheap spells plus green's protection and fight effects.
2. **Temur Crab.** Copy the Izzet Crab / Izzet Prowess package (Burst Lightning, Fiery Impulse, Prismari Charm) and add green for Bushwhack.
3. **Simic with a creature package from the menu,** such as Badgermole Cub or Stormchaser's Talent.

I chose Simic because Bushwhack's fight mode wants 5/5s, and green adds Ram Through, Snakeskin Veil and Stubborn Denial (a hard counter once you control a 4-power creature). Those cards make the big creatures better without needing a third colour.

**The plan**
- **Turns 1–2:** cast cantrips (Opt, Consider, Sleight of Hand, Bushwhack fetching a land) and Picklock Prankster's adventure side, which mills four. These fill the graveyard with instants and sorceries.
- **Turns 2–3:** cast Tolarian Terror (5/5, ward 2) for one to three mana. Its mana value is 7, so Fatal Push can't touch it.
- **Then:** Bushwhack or Ram Through lets the 5/5 kill their best creature. Eddymurk Crab has flash and can tap two blockers when it enters. Stubborn Denial and Spell Pierce protect the clock.

**Changes and trade-offs**
- **Fading Hope swapped out:** the deck checker said almost no recent Pioneer decks play it, so I replaced it with Boomerang Basics, which can also bounce Greasefang's vehicles and other non-creature permanents.
- **Ram Through kept:** the checker said players prefer Boomerang Basics here too, but Ram Through is a one-sided fight at instant speed. A 5/5 kills Sheoldred or Screaming Nemesis without taking damage back.
- **18 lands, against the checker's warning:** it suggests about 23 because it reads the two 7-drops at full cost. In practice they cost one to three mana. The deck also has 12 cantrips and Bushwhack's land-search mode.
- **Odds:** you'll see at least one Terror or Crab by turn 4 about 79% of the time. You'll see one of them together with Bushwhack or Ram Through about 53% of the time.
- **Sideboard:** aimed at the current field. It has graveyard hate (Unlicensed Hearse, Ghost Vacuum, Heritage Reclamation) for Greasefang and Phoenix, and Aether Gust for red and green decks. Counterspells (Negate, Disdainful Stroke, Mystical Dispute) cover control and midrange, and Tamiyo's Safekeeping protects your threats from removal.

--- After review ---
I took the reviewer's fix as suggested, and the resubmitted deck was accepted.

**What changed (main deck only):**
- **Cut all 3 Boomerang Basics.** It's a sorcery, and its "draw a card" half only works when you bounce your own permanent. The best own target is Picklock Prankster, so you can cast its Free the Fae half again. That's too slow and situational for a deck that wants to keep mana open on the opponent's turn.
- **Into the Flood Maw goes from 2 to 4.** It's instant-speed bounce for U and can only hit the opponent's permanents. Promising the gift lets it bounce any nonland permanent they control, not just a creature, though they get a tapped 1/1 Fish.
- **Added 1 Fading Hope.** It's an instant for U that bounces any creature, and scries 1 if that creature's mana value is 3 or less. You can cast it at the end of the opponent's turn alongside a flashed-in Eddymurk Crab.

**Why it doesn't hurt the plan:** all three new cards are instants, so the deck still has the same number of instants and sorceries to make Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab cheaper. Your plan to win is unchanged: cantrips and Prankster fill the graveyard, you cast a cheap Terror on turns 2–3, Bushwhack's fight mode clears a blocker, Crab adds a second 5/5, and Stubborn Denial protects them.

**Land count:** the checker warned that 18 lands is low and suggested about 23. That was already true before these changes, since the land base wasn't touched. Twelve 1-mana cantrips plus Bushwhack (which can fetch a land) make 18 workable, but it's on the lean side. If you keep stalling on two lands, swap a Spell Pierce or a Snakeskin Veil for a 19th land.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Riddlesmith, Ovalchase Daredevil and Echo of Eons.
results.text:
I built a Dimir artifact deck that takes the free-artifact base of Legacy's Affinity deck. Riddlesmith turns every cheap artifact you cast into a loot, and Ovalchase Daredevil is the card you discard that comes back. Echo of Eons is the refill once your hand is empty.

**How it works**
- **Early turns:** play Seat of the Synod, Mox Opal, Lotus Petal and Baubles on turn 1, then Riddlesmith on turn 2. After that, every artifact you cast lets you draw a card and then discard one.
- **Daredevil loop:** discard Daredevil to Riddlesmith's loot. The artifact you were casting then enters, which returns Daredevil to your hand. It's free fodder every turn, and a 4/2 you can cast when you need a body.
- **Monument to Endurance:** each discard lets you pick a different option once per turn: drain 3, make a Treasure or draw a card. The Treasure is an artifact, so it brings Daredevil back again. Underworld Cookbook can discard at instant speed, so you can drain on the opponent's turn too.
- **Echo of Eons:** once Affinity has dumped your hand, loot Echo away or mill it with Emry, Lurker of the Loch. Then cast it from the graveyard for {2}{U} to draw a new seven. It also wipes the opponent's hand and graveyard, which hurts Reanimator and decks holding Force of Will.
- **How you win:** Kappa Cannoneer gets a +1/+1 counter and can't be blocked whenever an artifact enters. Together with Patchwork Automaton, Urza's Saga Constructs, Daredevil beats and Monument drains, the deck aims to win around turn 5.

**Directions I considered**
1. **The Epic Storm (TES), the storm deck with Lion's Eye Diamond and Echo:** 87% of the real lists running these cards are TES. But TES only uses Echo, and it gives Riddlesmith and Daredevil nothing to do.
2. **A discard-value deck like Modern's Asmo Food** (Cookbook, Monument, Street Wraith): this is where Daredevil actually shows up in real lists. But it's too slow and fair for Legacy on its own.
3. **Dimir Affinity (my pick):** the Affinity base, plus the Cookbook and Monument package from option 2. I chose it because it is the one proven Legacy deck that casts and plays several artifacts every turn, and that is exactly what Riddlesmith and Daredevil need.

**Odds and caveats**
- This is an untested brew. No published list runs these three cards together.
- You'll have Riddlesmith or Cookbook by turn 3 about 64% of the time, and Daredevil about 39% of the time.
- The checker estimated a 0.4% chance of having drawn every card in the win sequence by turn 5. That counts all six cards; you don't need them all. The Affinity half (Kappa, Automaton, Saga) wins without the engine.
- I run 3 Daredevils and 2 Echoes rather than 4. One Daredevil in the graveyard keeps coming back, and Echo is clunky to draw in multiples.
- The checker flagged Cookbook because almost nobody plays it. I kept it: Urza's Saga can fetch it, and it's the second discard outlet that powers the Daredevil and Monument loops.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the current field: Tormod's Crypt, Dismember, Disruptor Flute, Consign to Memory, Force of Negation, Fatal Push and Sink into Stupor.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State.
results.text:
I built a Grixis (blue-black-red) "Buried Phoenix" combo brew. No published list runs these three cards together, so this is a new deck, not a known one.

**The plan.** Buried Alive puts three Arclight Phoenix straight into your graveyard. Buried Alive is a sorcery, so it counts toward the Phoenix's trigger: three instants or sorceries cast in one turn. The basic line:
1. Play a black land and cast Dark Ritual (instant #1, gives you BBB).
2. Cast Buried Alive (sorcery #2) and put three Phoenix in the graveyard.
3. Cast a third spell for no mana. Gut Shot costs 2 life instead of mana, and Mutagenic Growth works the same way.
4. At the start of combat, three 3/2 flying, haste Phoenixes come back and hit for 9. They stay on the battlefield and hit for 9 again the next turn.

**What Flow State does here.** It's a 2-mana sorcery, so it counts as one of the three spells. It digs for Buried Alive. Once Dark Ritual (an instant) and Buried Alive or Ponder (a sorcery) are in the graveyard, you keep two cards from the top three instead of one. Faithless Looting is a backup way to discard a Phoenix you've drawn into the graveyard.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **What I built:** a Phoenix combo deck. It borrows the fast mana and discard from Reanimator (Dark Ritual, Lotus Petal, Thoughtseize) and the blue cantrips, Force of Will and mana base from Doomsday.
2. Izzet Tempo with Phoenix as a creature and Buried Alive splashed in. Buried Alive does almost nothing in that deck.
3. A hybrid where Buried Alive also finds Griselbrand for Reanimate. Both plans get diluted.

I picked option 1 because Buried Alive plus three cheap spells is a real turn 1–2 kill. In the other two, the requested cards are just there for flavor.

**Honest odds and choices:**
- **How often it goes off:** You see Buried Alive by turn 3 only about 49% of the time without counting card draw. Brainstorm, Ponder, Flow State and Looting raise that a lot, but this is a fast, all-in deck, not a fair one.
- **Banned cards:** Entomb and Gitaxian Probe would fit perfectly, but both are banned in Legacy. Gut Shot and Mutagenic Growth are the free spells that replace them.
- **Land count:** I run 15 lands plus 4 Lotus Petal. The checker flagged 15 blue sources against about 19 in Doomsday lists. I accepted that because the deck's curve is so low (average mana value 1.8).
- **Sideboard:** It targets the tempo decks (Force of Negation, Pyroblast, more discard), creature decks (Abrade, Pyrokinesis) and graveyard combo (Tormod's Crypt, Surgical Extraction).

--- After review ---
I made the reviewer's fix: **-3 Mutagenic Growth, +3 Manamorphose**. The resubmitted deck was accepted with no warnings.

**Why:** The reviewer is right. Mutagenic Growth needs a creature to target, and on the combo turn the Phoenixes are still in the graveyard until combat. So it often had nothing to target, or only the opponent's creature. Manamorphose ({1}{R/G}, instant) needs no target. It gives back two mana of any colours and draws a card, so it counts as a spell for Arclight Phoenix and costs no net mana.

**Updated turn-2 line:** Two lands (one red source) cast Manamorphose, which makes BB. One of those B pays for Dark Ritual, which makes BBB. With the spare B that's BBBB, and Buried Alive uses three of it. That's three spells before combat, plus a drawn card. Three Phoenixes return with haste and flying for 9 damage, then 9 more the next turn. Gut Shot (paid with 2 life) can still replace any of the three spells, and Lotus Petal can stand in for the second land.

**One caveat:** submit_deck reported a 1.4% chance of having drawn every card in that exact line by turn 2. That number assumes no substitutes. In practice Gut Shot, Lotus Petal, Brainstorm and Ponder all fill in for missing pieces, so the real chance is higher. Even so, a turn-2 kill only happens with a good hand. A turn-3 kill is more typical.

I left everything else the same: lands, the rest of the main deck and the sideboard.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
This is a Boros artifact-weenie brew, accepted as legal at 60 cards with a 15-card sideboard. No published list in the last 400 days plays all three of your cards together, so the shell is borrowed from the Synthesizer archetype (Glint Hawk, Kor Skyfisher, Galvanic Blast, artifact lands).

**The plan:** Ancient Den, Great Furnace, Ornithopter, Springleaf Drum and Thraben Inspector's Clues reach three artifacts by turn 1–2. That turns Ardent Recruit and Auriok Sunchaser into 3/3s for one or two mana, and makes Galvanic Blast deal 4.

- **Springleaf Drum** taps any creature you control, even one you just cast, and Ornithopter is a free creature for it. The mana can be any color, so it also covers the red splash.
- **Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher** return Drum, Ornithopter, Synthesizer or an artifact land to your hand. Recasting them keeps the artifact count up and gets more value.
- **Search Party Captain** refills your hand. After an attack with Recruit, Hawk and Ornithopter (a 0/2 flyer is a safe attacker), it costs just W after combat and draws a card. Then Galvanic Blast clears a blocker or finishes the opponent.

**The sample win line** is: turn 1 Den + Ornithopter + Drum, turn 2 Recruit + Hawk, turn 3 a discounted Captain, then burn to win around turn 5. The deck doesn't need that exact sequence; it was built with lots of overlap. There are 22 artifact sources for metalcraft and 22 cheap creatures to discount the Captain. To be honest about consistency: you have about a 53% chance to draw a Drum by turn 4, and about the same for a Captain.

**Why this direction:** I compared three options:
- Mono-White Aggro with an artifact package added
- Orzhov Glintblade
- this Boros build

I chose Boros because Drum fixes for red, and Galvanic Blast rewards the same artifact count that Ardent Recruit needs. That gives the deck real removal and reach without weakening the aggro creatures.

**Sideboard:** It targets the decks currently at the top:
- **Terror and Faeries:** Red Elemental Blast
- **Elves and Mono-White go-wide:** Electrickery
- **Madness and other burn:** Prismatic Strands
- **Graveyard decks (Golgari Gardens, Spy Combo):** Relic of Progenitus
- **Affinity and Golgari Gardens' Ichor Wellspring/Lembas:** Gorilla Shaman
- **Big threats:** Journey to Nowhere

--- After review ---
I made the reviewer's change and resubmitted. The deck was accepted with no warnings.

**What changed:**
- **Out: 3 Wind-Scarred Crag. In: 3 Rustvale Bridge.** Both lands enter tapped and tap for R or W, so the colored mana doesn't change. The difference is that Bridge is an artifact land, so it counts toward the three artifacts that Ardent Recruit, Auriok Sunchaser and Galvanic Blast need. It's also indestructible, which covers it against removal that destroys artifacts. Crag's 1 life gain doesn't matter much in this deck.

**Artifact count after the swap:** 21 cards are artifacts themselves: 11 artifact lands (Ancient Den, Great Furnace, Rustvale Bridge), 4 Springleaf Drum, 3 Ornithopter and 3 Experimental Synthesizer. In the submitted needs I listed 25 sources, which also counts the 4 Thraben Inspector. Inspector isn't an artifact, but the Clue it makes is, so it helps a turn later.

The deck doesn't depend on drawing that exact sequence: any three artifacts turn on Recruit and Blast, and any cheap attackers make Captain cheaper.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a Boros (red-white) graveyard deck around a rule all three cards care about. Both Eidolons come back from your graveyard to your hand whenever you cast a multicolored spell, and hybrid cards like Boros Recruit count as multicolored. Spirit Mascot gets a +1/+1 counter every time cards leave your graveyard. No published list has run these three together, so this is a new build, not a copy of a proven deck.

**The plan:** Put Spirit Mascot down early. Use Thrilling Discovery, Faithless Looting and Pursue the Past to dig through your deck and discard the Eidolons on purpose. Then cast cheap multicolored creatures to bring the Eidolons back.
- Each Eidolon that returns puts a counter on Mascot. Each one is a separate trigger, so getting both back gives two counters.
- Flashback cards (Looting, Pursue the Past, Rally the Peasants) also leave the graveyard when you cast them, so Mascot grows again.
- Once the Eidolons are back, sacrifice them for what they do. Sandstorm Eidolon stops a blocker. Aurora Eidolon prevents 3 damage, so it can save Mascot from a Lightning Bolt. The next multicolored spell gets them back again.
- Rally the Peasants, cast and then flashed back, finishes the game around turn 6.

**How the line holds up:** There are 24 multicolored spells (Mascot, Boros Recruit, Wojek Halberdiers, Stonebound Mentor, Skyknight Legionnaire, Thrilling Discovery, Pursue the Past) and 8 discard cards that drop the Eidolons into the graveyard. The checker says you'll have drawn every card in my exact winning sequence by turn 6 only 1.7% of the time. That's the specific cards, though. Any multicolored spell can stand in for Stonebound Mentor, and any discard card can stand in for Thrilling Discovery, so the deck doesn't need that exact sequence.

**Three directions I looked at:**
1. Red-white graveyard deck, using the mana and the looting/flashback cards from the small Boros Aggro deck that shows up in results.
2. The Mono-White Aggro package (Kor Skyfisher, Battle Screech) with a little red added.
3. A red shell like Madness.

I chose the first, because it's the only one where the deck's spells actually trigger the Eidolons and Mascot. In the other two the requested cards would just be expensive filler.

**Things to know:**
- **Aurora Eidolon is at 3 copies, Sandstorm Eidolon at 4.** They're 4-mana 2/2s that keep coming back, so you rarely want several in hand.
- **Mana:** 18 lands with 12 white and 12 red sources. Boros Aggro lists run about 16 white sources, but this deck needs both colors evenly for Mascot and Mentor.
- **Sideboard (15):** Red Elemental Blast for Terror and Faeries, Electrickery for Elves and Mono-White, Dust to Dust for Affinity and Wildfire, plus Prismatic Strands, Journey to Nowhere and Thraben Charm.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Future Sight, Academy Rector and Veteran Explorer.
results.text:
I built **Bant Survival with a red splash for Goblin Bombardment**, focused on Academy Rector, Veteran Explorer and Future Sight. It's a brew: no recent list plays all three of your cards together.

**The plan:** Turn 1 Veteran Explorer. Once Goblin Bombardment is down, sacrifice the Explorer for 1 damage plus two basic lands (Island and Plains), which puts you at 4–5 mana by turn 3. Then sacrifice Academy Rector to Bombardment so it puts an enchantment into play for free: usually Future Sight, otherwise Opposition, Pattern of Rebirth or Survival of the Fittest. Future Sight lets you play lands and creatures off the top of your library every turn. That keeps feeding Survival (which finds Rector, Deranged Hermit, Squee or Palinchron) and Bombardment. The kill is Hermit's four 2/2 squirrels attacking, then all five bodies going to Bombardment. Squee comes back every turn for another point, and if Pattern of Rebirth fetches Symbiotic Wurm, that's 8 more damage. The line is built to finish around turn 6.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Pattern Combo shell.** This is the only real list that runs Rector with Explorer, but it's green-white-black-red with no blue. Adding Future Sight's three blue pips would make it a five-color mess.
2. **Blue-white enchantment control,** with Rector fetching Future Sight and Opposition. It has no real way to win and nothing that makes Explorer worth playing.
3. **Chosen: the green-blue core of Tradewind Survival** (Birds, Walls, Survival, Gaea's Cradle, Opposition, Tradewind Rider, Squee) with Pattern Combo's Rector + Bombardment package added. I picked it because green-blue gives Future Sight its blue mana, and Rector and Bombardment each need only one white or red. Bombardment also lets Rector and Explorer die exactly when you want them to.

**Things to know:**
- **Draw odds:** You'll see Rector, Future Sight or Survival by turn 3 about 86% of the time, and a Veteran Explorer about 49%.
- **Only three Future Sights:** Four Rectors, plus Survival finding Rector, are the main way it gets into play. A fourth copy at five mana would clog opening hands.
- **Sacrifice outlets:** Bombardment is the only real one. Without it, Rector and Explorer die by blocking or to the opponent's removal. The deck checker flagged Bombardment as a rarely played card. I kept it because it's the sacrifice engine and the win condition, not removal.
- **Mana:** 21 lands. There are fewer green-producing lands than Tradewind lists run (17 vs. about 22), traded for the white and blue Rector and Future Sight need. Six mana creatures and Explorer make up the difference.
- **Explorer feeds the opponent too:** they also search for two basics. That hurts most against Goblins and Sligh, so be careful about when you sacrifice it.

**Sideboard:** It's aimed at the decks winning right now:
- Swords to Plowshares and Hydroblast for Stiflenought, Goblins and Sligh.
- Xantid Swarm and Meddling Mage for counterspells and combo.
- Naturalize, Monk Realist and Tormod's Crypt for Enchantress and Replenish.
- Spike Feeder for the aggressive red decks.

--- After review ---
Both flags are fair. I'm making both fixes and resubmitting.

I made both of the reviewer's fixes and the revised deck was accepted. It's still a 60-card brew with the same Explorer → Bombardment → Rector → Future Sight → Hermit plan.

**What changed:**
1. **Palinchron out, second Deranged Hermit in.** The reviewer was right: Palinchron untaps lands, and that only matters with a loop or a mana sink, which this deck doesn't have. Hermit is the actual kill card (four squirrels attack, then five bodies go to Bombardment). With one copy, a single exiled or countered Hermit would leave both Survival and Pattern of Rebirth with no kill card to fetch. Two copies fixes that.
2. **Tradewind Rider out, fourth Goblin Bombardment in.** Rider needs creatures left alive to tap for it, and this deck wants to sacrifice them. Bombardment is the free sacrifice outlet that makes Explorer and Rector die when you want, so it's now a full four copies.

**Things to know:**
- The checker wanted at least 6 cards that kill your own creatures for Rector, and four Bombardments is below that. I kept four and explained why: Rector (1/2) and Explorer (1/1) also die blocking or to the opponent's removal, and their effects happen however they die. Wall of Blossoms, Survival and Future Sight help you dig for a Bombardment. A different outlet would have cost a Hermit or something for Rector to fetch.
- The checker reports that you'll almost never have drawn every card in the line by turn 6 (about 0% of games). That's expected, because it doesn't count tutors, and this deck finds its pieces with Survival, Rector and Pattern of Rebirth. Still, the turn-6 kill should be read as a good-draw target, not something that happens every game.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Utopia Tree, Rhystic Tutor and Bloodfire Colossus.
results.text:
I built **Jund Colossus Reanimator**, a brew. No published list plays these three cards together, so it borrows its reanimation package from Premodern's Reanimator deck and builds it around a black-green Survival engine with a red splash.

**The plan:** Never pay 8 mana for Bloodfire Colossus. Put it in the graveyard instead, either by fetching it with Survival of the Fittest and discarding it, or by discarding it to Putrid Imp. Then bring it back on turn 2–3 with Exhume or Animate Dead. It attacks as a 6/6. Once the opponent is at 6 or less, or when they try to remove it, pay R and sacrifice it to deal 6 to every creature and each player. That sacrifice also fixes Exhume's downside, because it kills whatever creature the opponent got back.

- **Utopia Tree:** Gets you to 4 mana on turn 3 and makes any color. That covers the black-green spells and the R the Colossus needs to sacrifice itself. Later in the game it's a creature to discard to Survival.
- **Rhystic Tutor:** The tax is the weak spot, so the deck plays around it. Cast early (often off Dark Ritual), the opponent usually can't pay 2. It finds whatever piece you're missing: Survival, Exhume or a Colossus.

**Directions I considered:**
1. Black-green Survival + Reanimator (chosen).
2. Utopia Tree ramping into Sneak Attack, which puts the Colossus in with haste.
3. Plugging the cards into the Hermit Druid combo deck from the menu.

I chose the first because it puts Colossus into play by turn 3 using proven reanimation cards. Sneak Attack is slower and needs Colossus in hand, and in Hermit Druid all three cards would just be filler.

**Odds and trade-offs:**
- **Setup odds:** On the play, you have a discard outlet or tutor plus a reanimation spell by turn 3 in about 73% of games.
- **The 3% figure:** The submission checker says all five cards in the win line are drawn by turn 5 in only about 3% of games. That number is misleading: those cards are interchangeable with Animate Dead, Imp, Buried Alive and the tutors, and the checker doesn't simulate tutors.
- **Land count:** I run 16 lands plus 4 Trees. That sits between Reanimator decks (about 14 lands) and the checker's suggestion of about 22, because Rhystic Tutor costs 3 and you'll sometimes cast Colossus the normal way.
- **Life total:** The sacrifice also hits you for 6. Don't Reanimate the Colossus unless you can afford losing 8 life, then 6 more.

The sideboard targets the decks on the menu: Pyroblast against Stiflenought, Pyroclasm against Goblins and Sligh, and Naturalize and Pernicious Deed against Enchantress. Xantid Swarm stops opponents from casting spells on the turn it attacks, which helps against counterspell decks. Snuff Out handles creatures.

--- After review ---
I changed one of the two flagged cards. The deck was accepted, but it has a land problem I haven't fixed (see below).

1. **Reanimate: cut, as the reviewer suggested.** The life math holds up: reanimating an 8-mana Colossus costs 8 life, and sacrificing it deals 6 more to you. Exhume and Animate Dead do the same job without the life loss. But the suggested replacement, Entomb, **is banned in Premodern**, so I couldn't add it. I put in **2 Wild Mongrel** instead. It discards a card for free (so the Colossus goes straight to the graveyard, like with Putrid Imp), it can be thrown away to pay for Survival of the Fittest, and it's a 2/2 that can attack.

2. **Buried Alive: kept, 2 copies.** The reviewer's point that it costs 3 mana is fair. But the suggested fix was Entomb again, and with Entomb banned, Buried Alive is the only legal card that puts the Colossus straight from the library into the graveyard. It doesn't need a second card in hand to discard, which is what Survival, Putrid Imp and Mongrel all need.

The deck now has 12 ways to get the Colossus into the graveyard (4 Survival, 4 Putrid Imp, 2 Wild Mongrel, 2 Buried Alive) and 8 ways to bring it back (4 Exhume, 4 Animate Dead). The win plan is unchanged: Colossus comes back on turn 3.

**Two problems you should know about:**
- **Too few lands.** The deck runs 16 lands, and the checker says Premodern decks with this curve usually run about 22. Utopia Tree and Dark Ritual cover part of that, but expect to miss land drops sometimes. If that happens a lot, cut Duress or Cabal Therapy for lands.
- **The odds of drawing the whole line by turn 3 are low.** The tool found that you draw every card in the turn-3 line in about 1% of games. That number doesn't count Rhystic Tutor or Survival of the Fittest finding missing pieces, so the real chance is higher. I can't say how much higher.
